analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third-person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־

analysis.sense: The personal name of Abel’s brother.

analysis.evidence: In וַיֹּאמֶר קַיִן אֶל הֶבֶל אָחִיו, אֶל introduces Abel, the brother to whom Cain spoke.
In וַיֹּאמֶר קַיִן אֶל הֶבֶל אָחִיו, the preposition אֶל introduces Abel as the person Cain addresses. The appositive אָחִיו identifies him as Cain’s brother.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular proper noun in the absolute state, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In וַיֹּאמֶר קַיִן אֶל הֶבֶל אָחִיו, אָחִיו stands in apposition to הֶבֶל. The suffix refers to Cain, identifying Abel as Cain’s brother.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular construct noun with a third-person masculine singular possessive suffix.

analysis.evidence: וַיְהִי introduces the event impersonally. בִּהְיוֹתָם בַּשָּׂדֶה gives its setting, “while they were in the field,” and וַיָּקָם קַיִן begins the account of what happened, “Cain rose up.”
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, third person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־ and no suffix

analysis.evidence: The suffix refers to Cain and Abel. The following בַּשָּׂדֶה supplies their location, so בִּהְיוֹתָם בַּשָּׂדֶה means “while they were in the field” and sets the scene for Cain’s attack.
analysis.morphology: Temporal preposition בְּ + Qal infinitive construct הֱיוֹת + third-person masculine plural suffix ם marking the subject.

analysis.evidence: בִּהְיוֹתָם בַּשָּׂדֶה means “while they were in the field.” The phrase locates Cain and Abel in the open country when Cain rose against his brother.
analysis.morphology: Preposition בְּ with the definite article הַ, followed by a masculine singular absolute noun.
analysis.sense: open country, the land outside town and house

analysis.evidence: In וַיָּקָם קַיִן אֶל הֶבֶל אָחִיו, אֶל marks Abel as the person against whom Cain rose. The following וַיַּהַרְגֵהוּ, “and he killed him,” confirms the hostile sense.
In וַיָּקָם קַיִן אֶל הֶבֶל אָחִיו, Cain rises against Abel. The appositive אָחִיו (“his brother”) identifies Abel as Cain’s brother.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular proper noun, without prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: Cain is the subject of וַיָּקָם and remains the subject of וַיַּהַרְגֵהוּ. The object suffix refers to הֶבֶל אָחִיו, “Abel his brother,” whom Cain rose against and killed.
analysis.morphology: Qal wayyiqtol, 3rd person masculine singular, with prefixed וַ־ and 3rd person masculine singular object suffix ־ֵהוּ.
